title: Strings — Working With Text
description: Manipulate and analyse text with Python's powerful string tools.

sections.content: Strings are sequences of characters. Python has many built-in tools for working with them. You can count characters, convert case, search inside text, and split it into pieces.

sections.code:
message = "Hello, Myanmar!"

print(len(message))           # 15 — number of characters
print(message.upper())        # HELLO, MYANMAR!
print(message.lower())        # hello, myanmar!
print(message.replace("Hello", "Mingalaba"))  # Mingalaba, Myanmar!
sections.explanation: String methods are called with a dot after the variable name. upper() and lower() change the case. replace() swaps one piece of text for another. These all return new strings — the original is unchanged.

sections.code:
sentence = "Python is fun to learn"

print(sentence.split())          # ['Python', 'is', 'fun', 'to', 'learn']
print(sentence.split("to"))      # ['Python is fun ', ' learn']

words = sentence.split()
print(len(words))                # 5 — number of words
sections.explanation: split() breaks a string into a list of parts. With no argument, it splits on spaces. With an argument, it splits on that specific text.

sections.question:
What will this print?
name = "  khin myo  "
print(name.strip().title())
sections.explanation: strip() removes leading and trailing spaces. title() capitalises the first letter of each word. Together: 'Khin Myo'.

sections.code:
# Slicing — getting part of a string
text = "Hello, World!"

print(text[0:5])   # Hello   (characters 0 to 4)
print(text[7:])    # World!  (from index 7 to end)
print(text[:5])    # Hello   (from start to index 4)
print(text[-6:])   # World!  (last 6 characters)
sections.explanation: text[start:end] gives you a slice of the string. The end index is not included. Negative indices count from the end: -1 is the last character.

sections.prompt:
Write a program that takes a full name from the user and prints:
1. The name in all capitals
2. The number of characters in the name (not counting spaces)
3. The initials (first letter of each word)
sections.starterCode:
name = input("Enter your full name: ")

# 1. Print in capitals

# 2. Print number of characters (not counting spaces)

# 3. Print initials (first letter of each word)
sections.hint: For initials: split the name into words, then for each word take word[0].
sections.solution:
name = input("Enter your full name: ")

# 1. Capitals
print(name.upper())

# 2. Characters without spaces
no_spaces = name.replace(" ", "")
print(len(no_spaces))

# 3. Initials
words = name.split()
initials = ""
for word in words:
    initials += word[0].upper()
print(initials)
